steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Aggression: Behaviour that is intended to harm another person or object. In sport, aggression must be distinguished from assertion - assertion is forceful but legitimate play within the rules, while aggression goes beyond the rules with intent to harm. | Direct Aggression: Aggression that is aimed directly at another person, involving physical contact or confrontation with the intent to cause harm. | Indirect Aggression: Aggression that is not aimed directly at another person. It may involve verbal abuse, psychological intimidation, or aggression directed at objects rather than people. | Personality: The unique combination of characteristics, traits and behaviours that make an individual distinct.
